{
  "markdown_report": "Choose a **serving-aligned candidate composition audit** before changing BERT4Rec’s training objective. At 0% progress, this provides a feasible descriptive experiment without additional fitted predictors; it does not establish a training improvement.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. Earlier serving checks passed, while another adapter lacked routing and replay inputs; availability must be verified for the current checkpoint. Recent deletion reduced target scores, but diagnostic hit-rate intervals included zero; sensitivity does not establish useful temporal prediction. Feedback distinguishes immediate choice, deferred relevance and unidentified items; none supplies verified negative relevance labels or unobserved compatibility/mood information.

Three literature insights guide the design. Sampled rankings can reverse model comparisons, and different candidate samplers define different tasks [1]. Sequential-recommendation sampling studies motivate frequency controls [2,4]. BERT4Rec requires masked targets and appended-MASK scoring [3]; historical training-prefix targets nevertheless remain in-sample [5].

| Direction | Controlled comparison | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Execution validity | Current versus exported checkpoint scores | Untested production paths |
| Candidate composition | Uniform, target-frequency-matched, lexical and lexical-frequency-matched sets | Unknown relevance and selected support |
| Temporal specificity | Fixed-candidate history perturbations | Sensitivity is not usefulness |

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate composition audit [1,2,4] | 4/6/5 | Useful synthesis; reusable controls; existing scorer suffices | Established techniques; uncertain training benefit; matching and integration add work |
| Anchored older-history shuffle [3] | 3/5/3 | Focused order hypothesis; supports temporal studies; simple perturbation | Familiar intervention; inconclusive effects possible; position controls matter |
| Evidence-linked feedback labels | 3/6/4 | Separates abstention from rejection; improves annotation; no model change | Conventional taxonomy; twenty users limit inference; coding needs review |

For the selected audit, freeze checkpoint, users, historical prefixes, targets, exclusions and tie handling. Compare target-plus-99-unique-candidate sets: uniform, target-frequency-band matched, lexical neighbors, and nonlexical candidates matching each lexical draw’s frequency-band histogram. The fourth regime narrows frequency confounding; matching remains coarse and does not establish semantic causation.

Use training-only frequencies and local sparse TF-IDF over permitted titles/descriptions. Retain positive similarities, deterministic score/item-ID ordering, and three seeded draws. Report shortages and text coverage; paired contrasts use a shared text-eligible population and common available endpoints. Report missing-text results separately. Unobserved candidates may be relevant alternatives.

Compute B×L×D features once per prefix, gather the final MASK query, and score through the trained head with explicit B×K candidate alignment. Never use count-minus-one indexing or replace the scoring head with embedding dot products.

Report target ranks, target-minus-tenth-negative margins, hit flips and draw variability. Bootstrap users within category, retaining paired draws, then recompute equal-category macro contrasts only when all four categories are available. Intervals condition on fitted models and selected support; they exclude training/search uncertainty and do not repair selection bias [6].

Preserve interfaces, state restoration, compute caps, four routes, seeds, limits and predictor consistency. Deploy one BERT4Rec checkpoint/category. Select solely through unchanged host macro validation HR@10; no improvement is established.

[1](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) · [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) · [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) · [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045) · [5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060) · [6](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v48/schnabel16.html)",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Add a serving-aligned candidate composition audit to the corrected BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter. Compare fixed public historical training-prefix targets under uniform, target-frequency-band-matched, lexical-neighbor and lexical-frequency-histogram-matched candidate sets. Score every candidate exclusively with the category’s single trained BERT4Rec; all retrieval and frequency calculations remain diagnostic-only.",
    "motivation": "The supplied diagnostics and qualitative feedback establish neither a training repair nor a semantic discrimination defect. Candidate construction affects sampled rankings, while lexical neighborhoods also change popularity and text coverage. A fourth frequency-matched control and common-support comparisons narrow these confounders. Differences remain retrospective sensitivity measurements for a fixed checkpoint, not evidence of improved learning, compatibility reasoning or recommendation quality. At 0% progress, this audit is preferable to a complex optimizer-transfer intervention; anchored shuffling and evidence-linked feedback coding remain useful subsequent directions.",
    "implementation_notes": "Keep the corrected baseline training and scoring architecture unchanged for this experiment. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch, and every ModelView interface. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Pass actual category identity from the training loop; do not infer it from item counts. The loader contract remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Capture at most ten independently cloned batches already consumed by training for existing sampler/margin probes; do not advance the live training iterator to populate replay. Run probes independently and retain completed results with definitions, counts, statuses and specific failure reasons. Missing replay blocks only dependent probes. Undefined measurements are null, never healthy zero-valued defaults.

Before interpreting scoring results, verify exact state-tensor identity between the current serialized category checkpoint and view.model, authoritative routing and item-ID mapping, and finite internal/exported appended-MASK scores on short, full-length, truncated and batched histories. Use atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, plus identical diagnostic ordered rankings. A previous run’s parity result is insufficient. Missing evidence makes affected comparisons unavailable; it does not establish a serving defect. Preserve final-nonpadding readout using the maximum valid position index, never nonpadding-count minus one. Canonical construction truncates history to maxlen-1, appends MASK, then left-pads to maxlen, so its query is at maxlen-1. Preserve PAD=0 and reserved MASK=itemnum+1; neither is a candidate.

Specify scoring shapes explicitly. log2feats(sequence) returns B x L x D. Gather query=features[batch_indices, mask_positions], yielding B x D. For B x K item IDs, use the actual trained scoring head, including transformations and biases. Implement a family-specific diagnostic wrapper around predict_score according to its existing contract: either broadcast B x 1 x D queries against B x K candidates or explicitly expand queries to B x K x D when aligned-position inputs are required. Assert B x K finite output and verify equivalence to independently scored candidates and exported prediction. Never assume the supplied interface accepts arbitrary broadcasting, score the whole B x L sequence against K candidates implicitly, or replace its trained head with a raw embedding dot product. Position-wise B x L positive/negative labels must be gathered with the same batch/position indices as their queries.

Select up to 32 eligible users/category with a dedicated seed-42 generator before examining scores, and one uniformly selected eligible endpoint/user. Require at least four preceding interactions and a target absent from the complete preceding prefix. Freeze selected endpoints before computing regime-specific eligibility; do not replace excluded users to obtain favorable coverage. Construct input solely from that prefix’s final maxlen-1 items plus MASK. Later interactions never enter the input or determine candidate exclusions. Count invalid IDs and all eligibility failures. These targets occurred in model fitting: masking them now does not remove memorization or establish temporal generalization.

Compute retrospective item frequencies from complete public training histories only. Freeze bands [1,4), [4,16), [16,64), [64,256), [256,infinity), plus a separate zero-frequency band. These counts describe full-training popularity, not popularity known at the historical target time. No temporal-validity claim follows. If a later diagnostic adds time-local counts, it must define strictly-before-target timestamps, window and denominator; this does not make the existing fitted model temporally restricted.

Keep catalog rows in ascending real item-ID order. Join permitted title and description fields using a fixed whitespace separator, treating absent fields as empty. Fit one sklearn TfidfVectorizer per category with lowercase=True, analyzer='word', token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b', ngram_range=(1,1), min_df=1, max_df=1.0, max_features=50000, norm='l2', use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, sublinear_tf=False and dtype=float32. Record library versions, vocabulary and catalog-text fingerprints. Reuse that vocabulary for targets. Empty/tokenless rows have no lexical evidence; an entirely empty fitting vocabulary makes lexical probes unavailable with an explicit reason. Compute only target-to-catalog or small target-batch sparse similarities using cosine_similarity(Q, X, dense_output=False); never allocate catalog-by-catalog similarities. CPU text preparation is measured separately from GPU work.

Define E as all real catalog items excluding the target and every item in the complete preceding prefix. Define E_text as members of E with nonzero TF-IDF rows. Retain the original all-catalog uniform and target-frequency-band regimes as descriptive coverage results, but use E_text for the primary four-regime comparisons. Their primary endpoints also require a nonzero target text row. Report missing-text endpoints and all-catalog results separately. Complete-case contrasts describe selected text-supported users and items, not the full population.

Each regime contains one target and 99 unique negatives. Primary uniform draws are uniform without replacement from E_text. Target-frequency-matched draws are uniform without replacement from the subset of E_text in the target's frozen frequency band; this is not popularity-proportional sampling. Lexical draws use strictly positive target similarity, exclude ineligible IDs, order by descending similarity then ascending item ID with np.lexsort((item_ids, -scores)), retain the first 500, and sample 99 uniformly without replacement. Fewer than 99 positive-similarity neighbors makes the regime unavailable; do not fill with zero-similarity items or silently relax matching. TF-IDF similarity is neither compatibility nor verified substitutability.

Add a lexical-frequency-histogram-matched control for every available lexical draw. Count that draw's 99 negatives in the frozen frequency bands. For each band, sample the identical count uniformly without replacement from E_text after excluding the entire positive-similarity top-500 lexical pool. This gives a less lexically concentrated control with exactly matched coarse frequency counts. If any band has insufficient support, record the unavailable control and deficient counts; do not widen bands, reuse items or change the lexical draw. Excluding the lexical pool changes support, so label this a matched composition contrast, not a pure causal effect of semantics. Residual within-band frequency, text length, exposure and relevance differences remain possible explanations. Report per-band frequency summaries for both sets.

Use three predefined draws per endpoint/regime. Use numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence([42, category_index, selected_user_index, endpoint_index, draw_index, regime_index, band_index]))) with fixed category/regime ordering and zero band_index for unstratified draws; record indices and sampled item IDs. Do not use process-randomized Python hash values. The histogram control is paired to its lexical draw. Freeze checkpoint, input histories, targets, candidate count, complete-prefix exclusions and tie handling across regimes; candidate identities change by design. If a later experiment compares two scoring methods, use identical candidate IDs for both methods within every target/draw/regime. Do not conflate this requirement with holding candidates fixed across sampler contrasts.

Compute sequence features once per endpoint or endpoint batch in evaluation mode without gradients and reuse queries across candidate regimes. Score candidates in chunks if necessary. Rank with descending neural score then ascending item ID for diagnostic reproducibility; leave host tie handling unchanged. Report raw one-based target rank, target-minus-tenth-highest-negative margin, diagnostic hit@10 and paired hit flips. For exactly 99 negatives, the tenth-highest-negative score defines the margin; when scores tie, report the margin and separately apply the declared item-ID rank rule. Also report the percentile (rank-1)/99, explicitly labeling it the fraction of sampled negatives ahead under that tie rule, not a full-catalog rank estimate.

For each contrast, use endpoints with all three completed paired draws in both regimes; retain partial raw records separately. Report per-regime eligible users, targets, draws, missingness reasons and contrast-specific complete-case denominators. Publish a secondary all-four-regime common-support comparison when available. Report means by category, frozen training-frequency band and visible-history bins [4,8), [8,16), [16,32), [32,infinity); sparse strata retain counts and unavailable statistics rather than invented conclusions. Do not tune bands or bins after inspecting outcomes.

Average each user's paired contrast across its three draws, then average users equally within category. For descriptive user uncertainty, use 500 bootstrap replicates with a dedicated seed-42 stream, resampling users within category and retaining their complete paired draw records. Recompute the equally weighted four-category macro contrast in every replicate only when all four category results are present; a single-category ModelView must return macro unavailable. Report candidate-draw variability separately as the three per-draw contrast means and their descriptive standard deviation/range. These are different uncertainty sources; do not present a user-only interval as incorporating candidate-sampling uncertainty. With only three draws, Monte Carlo variability is coarsely measured. Intervals condition on checkpoint, selected support and fixed draws, exclude training/search uncertainty, assume independent user clusters and may omit shared-item dependence. Bootstrap cannot repair regime-dependent selection bias. Do not invent propensities or claim that weighting automatically corrects nonlinear sampled HR@10.

Full-catalog target ranks remain an optional descriptive reference only if included in a separately declared affordable cap before execution; otherwise mark them unrun. They would still measure retrospective in-sample target retrieval with unknown alternative relevance. Repeated candidate draws do not make sampled HR@10 equivalent to full-catalog HR@10. Lower target hits among lexical alternatives may reflect competing relevant items rather than worse recommendations.

Predeclare a 15-second soft GPU audit cap/category. Measure CUDA execution with synchronization/events and record CPU preparation, synchronized scoring wall time, completed users/draws, failures and cap overruns. A soft cap checked between operations can overrun during an in-flight operation. Bound CPU preparation separately in the protocol and report interruption/partial completion explicitly. Include all training, diagnostics, debugging and failures within the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget; do not promise additional training arms or affordable full-catalog reference runs without runtime evidence.

Use evaluation mode and no gradients. Restore each module's individual mode and controlled Python/NumPy/Torch CPU/CUDA RNG state in finally blocks. Use dedicated diagnostic streams and read-only cloned inputs. Audit the known corrected model's forward behavior and hooks for mutable state; protect identified mutable buffers and remove only diagnostic-owned hooks. A disposable copy of the same checkpoint may be used solely for diagnostics when needed, without fitting or deployment. Do not impose hypothetical arbitrary-hook concerns as blanket gates on otherwise audited valid probes. Record unavailable isolation guarantees accurately. Preserve existing valid embedding, sampler, margin and behavioral measurements with their definitions; embedding alignment is not proof of collapse or recommendation quality, and positive training margins do not establish convergence.

Generate diagnosis_interpreter_prompt directly from measured metrics, definitions, denominators, coverage, uncertainty scope, statuses and costs. Distinguish unavailable measurements from unobserved user-item relevance; neither means dislike. Keep immediate choice, explicitly deferred relevance, explicit incompatibility/duplication, explicit preference reversal and unidentified-item abstention separate when describing the twenty-user feedback. Ground annotations in exact feedback spans and identified items; use independent coding where feasible and report disagreement. Do not infer equipment ownership, mood, quantity needs or specifications without explicit permitted evidence. These annotations remain hypothesis-generating and are not validation labels.

Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches/epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five designated real training users/category. Each category trains and loads exactly one model/checkpoint. No ensembles, independently fitted auxiliary scoring models, score fusion, checkpoint averaging, pretrained weights, hidden test access or cross-trial checkpoint reuse. TF-IDF is fitted only for diagnostic candidate construction and contributes no deployed scores. Keep checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer synchronized. Only the unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10 determines selection. Audit outcomes must not trigger adaptive candidate redesign, checkpoint choice or item-specific ranking rules; any later training hypothesis requires a separately declared experiment. No validation improvement is established by this proposal.",
    "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        metrics, definitions = {}, {}
        saved = capture_audited_diagnostic_state(self.view.model)
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            # Uses independently cloned already-consumed replay batches.
            run_existing_probes_independently(metrics, definitions, train_loader)
            parity = verify_current_checkpoint_routing_mapping_and_export(self.view)
            metrics['serving_parity'] = parity
            if not parity.passed:
                metrics['candidate_audit'] = unavailable(parity.reason)
                return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

            frequencies = count_public_training_interactions(self.view.user_train)
            bands = fixed_frequency_bands(frequencies)
            catalog = real_items_in_ascending_id_order()
            X, text_status = fit_declared_sparse_tfidf(catalog)
            endpoints = select_fixed_training_endpoints(seed=42, limit=32)

            with torch.no_grad():
                for endpoint in endpoints:
                    if declared_audit_cap_reached():
                        record_partial_completion()
                        break
                    prefix, target = endpoint.prefix, endpoint.target
                    x = left_pad(prefix[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK], maxlen)
                    F = self.view.log2feats(x)  # B x L x D
                    p = actual_final_mask_positions(x)
                    q = F[torch.arange(F.shape[0], device=F.device), p]  # B x D
                    assert torch.all(p == maxlen-1)
                    E = real_catalog_excluding_complete_prefix_and_target(prefix, target)
                    E_text = eligible_nonzero_text_rows(E, X)
                    lexical_pool = sparse_positive_neighbors(
                        target, X, eligible=E_text, limit=500,
                        order='descending_similarity_then_ascending_item_id')

                    for draw in range(3):
                        sets = {}
                        sets['uniform_all_catalog'] = seeded_sample(E, 99)
                        sets['target_band_all_catalog'] = seeded_sample(
                            E_in_target_band(E, target, bands), 99)
                        if target_has_nonzero_text(target, X):
                            sets['uniform'] = seeded_sample(E_text, 99)
                            sets['target_band'] = seeded_sample(
                                E_in_target_band(E_text, target, bands), 99)
                            sets['lexical'] = seeded_sample(lexical_pool, 99)
                            if sets['lexical'].available:
                                histogram = band_counts(sets['lexical'], bands)
                                sets['lexical_frequency_control'] = sample_exact_band_counts(
                                    E_text.difference(lexical_pool), histogram,
                                    seeds=declared_seed_sequences(endpoint, draw))
                        else:
                            record_primary_text_population_unavailable(endpoint)

                        for regime, negatives in sets.items():
                            if negatives.unavailable:
                                record_unavailable(regime, negatives.reason,
                                                   negatives.support_counts)
                                continue
                            if declared_audit_cap_reached():
                                record_partial_completion()
                                break
                            ids = batch_candidate_ids([target] + negatives.items)  # B x 100
                            # Wrapper preserves the actual trained scoring head and its
                            # existing predict_score alignment/broadcasting contract.
                            scores = score_queries_with_verified_family_head(q, ids)
                            assert scores.shape == ids.shape and scores.isfinite().all()
                            record_ids_scores_rank_margin_hit_and_cost(
                                endpoint, draw, regime, ids, scores)

            metrics['candidate_audit'] = summarize_complete_paired_user_draws(
                require_draws=3, retain_partial_records=True,
                user_bootstrap_replicates=500,
                report_draw_variability_separately=True,
                macro_only_if_all_four_categories_present=True)
            attach_all_metric_definitions_counts_coverage_and_costs(metrics, definitions)
            return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            remove_only_diagnostic_owned_hooks()
            restore_audited_state_and_individual_module_modes(self.view.model, saved)
            restore_controlled_rng_states_last(saved)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return render_measured_metrics_definitions_counts_and_availability(
        raw_diagnosis,
        instruction='Describe retrospective candidate-composition sensitivity, '
                    'selected support, unknown candidate relevance and uncertainty limits. '
                    'Do not infer dislike, compatibility, mood, semantic causation, '
                    'temporal generalization or host validation improvement.')

# Train/export exactly one unchanged corrected BERT4Rec per required category.
# TF-IDF and frequency controls select audit candidates only.
# Deployed predictions use only the category checkpoint's trained neural scoring head.",
    "originality": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "Combines serving-aligned BERT4Rec checks, shared text support and a lexical-frequency-histogram control into a focused diagnostic protocol.",
      "negative": "Sampling audits, frequency matching, sparse lexical retrieval and clustered uncertainty are established methods; the contribution is a task-specific synthesis."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 6,
      "positive": "Can support narrower subsequent sampling or discrimination hypotheses and provide reusable coverage-aware diagnostics across all four categories.",
      "negative": "Retrospective candidate sensitivity may not identify an effective training change, and unknown relevance prevents interpreting lexical difficulty as worse recommendation quality."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 5,
      "positive": "Reuses one trained encoder and scoring head per category, with no additional training or deployed architecture changes.",
      "negative": "Verified scoring shapes, current-export parity, sparse retrieval, matched support shortages, deterministic draws and cross-category paired aggregation require more integration than the original rating of three suggested."
    }
  },
